questions.question: Which mountain pass connects Ladakh with Kashmir Valley?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zoji La**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Zoji La** is a high-altitude mountain pass located in the **Himalayan Range** within the Union Territory of **Ladakh**, India.
 
• It serves as the vital geographical link between the **Kashmir Valley** (specifically near **Sonamarg**) and the **Ladakh** region, providing access to **Drass**, **Kargil**, and **Leh**.
 
• The pass is situated at an approximate elevation of **3,528 meters** (**11,575 feet**) above sea level, making it one of the most dangerous and strategically important passes in the world.
 
• It is a critical component of **National Highway 1** (NH 1), which facilitates the movement of supplies and military personnel between **Srinagar** and **Leh**.
 
• Due to extreme weather conditions and heavy snowfall, the pass remains closed for nearly six months every year, leading to the development of the **Zojila Tunnel** to provide year-round connectivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nathu La**:

 
 
• Located in the **East Sikkim** district of the Indian state of **Sikkim**.
 
• It connects India with the **Tibet Autonomous Region** of China and was a major artery of the ancient **Silk Road**.
 
 
 
• **Rohtang Pass**:
 
 
• Situated in the **Pir Panjal Range** of the Himalayas in **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• It connects the **Kullu Valley** with the high-altitude **Lahaul and Spiti Valleys**.
 
 
 
• **Shipki La**:
 
 
• Located in the **Kinnaur** district of **Himachal Pradesh** on the Indo-China border.
 
• It is the point where the **Sutlej River** enters India from Tibet.

questions.question: Xuanzang's account is particularly valuable for the study of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harshavardhana's court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xuanzang**, a prominent **Chinese Buddhist monk** and traveler, visited India during the **7th Century CE** (specifically between **629–645 CE**) during the reign of **King Harshavardhana**.
 
• His famous travelogue, **Si-Yu-Ki** (Record of the Western World), provides a comprehensive eye-witness account of the **political, social, and economic conditions** of the **Vardhana Empire**.
 
• He spent several years at **Harshavardhana's court** and at **Nalanda University**, where he studied under the guidance of the monk **Shilabhadra**, documenting the high standards of education and religious debates of that era.
 
• The monk vividly describes the **Kannauj Assembly** and the **Prayag Assembly**, highlighting Harsha's religious tolerance and his massive patronage of **Mahayana Buddhism** and public welfare.
 
• Xuanzang’s records are essential for understanding the transition from the ancient to the early medieval period in India, particularly regarding the **administration** and the city of **Kannauj**, which served as the imperial capital.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Comparison with other historical periods mentioned in the options:
 
 
• **Harappan towns**: This **Indus Valley Civilization** flourished during the **Bronze Age** (c. 3300–1300 BCE); knowledge of this period is based entirely on **archaeological excavations** at sites like **Mohenjo-daro** and **Harappa**.
 
• **Mauryan polity**: This era (c. 322–185 BCE) is primarily studied through **Kautilya’s Arthashastra**, the **Indica** by the Greek ambassador **Megasthenes**, and the **Edicts of Ashoka**.
 
• **Chola naval expeditions**: These were prominent during the **10th and 11th Centuries CE** under rulers like **Rajaraja I** and **Rajendra Chola I**; they are documented in **Tamil inscriptions** and copper plates, long after Xuanzang's return to China.

questions.concept: India under East India Company’s Rule
questions.question: The Charter Act of 1813 ended the East India Company's monopoly over?

options.text: Trade with India, except tea and China trade

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Trade with India, except tea and China trade**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Charter Act of 1813**, also known as the **East India Company Act 1813**, was enacted by the **British Parliament** to renew the **East India Company's (EIC)** charter for another **20 years**.
 
• A landmark provision of this Act was the **abolition of the trade monopoly** of the Company in **India**, effectively opening **Indian trade** to all **British merchants** and private traders.
 
• Despite the liberalization of general trade, the **East India Company** retained its **exclusive monopoly** over the **tea trade** and all commercial **trade with China**.
 
• The shift toward **Free Trade** was largely influenced by the **Napoleonic Wars** and the **Continental System**, which restricted British access to **European markets** and forced the search for new economic avenues in **Asia**.
 
• The Act was significant for formally asserting the **sovereignty of the British Crown** over the territories held by the Company in **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Educational and Religious Impact**:

 
 
• The Act authorized **Christian Missionaries** to travel to **India** for the purpose of religious proselytization and moral improvement of the native population.
 
• It mandated the Company to set aside a sum of **1 lakh rupees** annually for the **promotion of education**, literature, and the **knowledge of sciences** among the inhabitants of British India.
 
 
 
• **Transition to 1833**:
 
 
• The **Charter Act of 1833** later removed the remaining **monopolies on tea** and **trade with China**, transforming the **East India Company** into a purely **administrative and political body**.
 
• It also led to the centralization of administration, making the **Governor-General of Bengal** the **Governor-General of India**.
 
 
 
• **Commercial Accountability**:
 
 
• The 1813 Act required the Company to maintain separate accounts for its **commercial transactions** and its **territorial revenues** to ensure better financial transparency for the **British Parliament**.

questions.question: Which Indian state government launched the scheme in 2025 'Mukhyamantri Balika Samridhi Yojana'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tripura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mukhyamantri Balika Samridhi Yojana** is a significant welfare initiative launched by the **Government of Tripura** in **2025** aimed at the socio-economic empowerment of the girl child.
 
• The scheme is designed to provide financial security to girls belonging to households classified under the **Below Poverty Line (BPL)** category, ensuring they have access to better healthcare and education.
 
• A primary goal of the scheme is the eradication of **child marriage**; therefore, the disbursement of the financial corpus is strictly contingent upon the girl remaining unmarried until she reaches the age of **18 years**.
 
• It focuses on improving the **Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER)** for girls by providing staggered financial incentives at various educational milestones, thereby reducing the **dropout rate** in secondary education.
 
• By incentivizing the birth of a girl child, the **Tripura** government aims to positively influence the **Child Sex Ratio** and address gender-based discrimination in the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Departmental Role and Implementation**:

 
 
• The **Department of Social Welfare and Social Education** serves as the nodal agency for the execution and regular monitoring of the **Mukhyamantri Balika Samridhi Yojana**.
 
• Transparency in the scheme is maintained through the **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** mechanism, where funds are credited directly to the bank accounts of the eligible beneficiaries.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Alignment**:
 
 
• The initiative aligns with the national **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao** campaign, reinforcing the pillars of survival, protection, and education for girls across **North-East India**.
 
• It contributes significantly toward achieving **Sustainable Development Goal 5 (SDG 5)**, which focuses on gender equality, and **SDG 4**, which emphasizes quality education for all.
 
• The scheme complements other financial instruments like the **Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana**, providing a robust safety net for young women in **Tripura**.

questions.question:
Which of the following is correct regarding the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill passed by Lok Sabha in August 2025?

I. The bill encourages e-sports and online social games. 

II. The bill also encourages online money gaming services.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Bill**, discussed in the **Lok Sabha**, seeks to establish a formal framework to categorize and govern the rapidly expanding digital gaming sector in India. It prioritizes the growth of the **Animation, Visual Effects, Gaming, and Comics (AVGC)** sector as a key driver of the **digital economy**.
 
• Statement I is accurate as the bill specifically emphasizes the promotion of **e-sports** and **online social games**. By recognizing **e-sports** as a professional competitive field, the bill facilitates **infrastructure development**, **international participation**, and **talent scouting** within a structured environment. *Hence, statement I is correct.*
 
• Online **social games**, which do not involve any real-money wagering, are encouraged to promote **indigenous culture** and **educational content** through gaming, aligning with the **Digital India** mission. *Hence, statement I is correct.*
 
• Statement II is inaccurate because the bill is designed to **regulate** and **restrict**, rather than **encourage**, **online money gaming**. The legislation introduces a strict distinction between **games of skill** and **games of chance**, imposing rigorous **KYC (Know Your Customer)** requirements and **financial audits** to prevent **money laundering** and **illegal betting**.
 
• The regulatory framework for money gaming focuses on **consumer protection** and mitigating **gaming addiction**. It mandates the appointment of a **Grievance Redressal Officer** and a **Chief Compliance Officer** for platforms offering monetary stakes, ensuring they operate under tight surveillance rather than broad encouragement. *Hence, statement II is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **E-sports vs. Online Money Gaming**:

 
 
• **E-sports**: These are skill-based, organized competitions often played at professional levels. The bill aims to provide these athletes with the same status as traditional sports players to enhance India's presence in **global gaming tournaments** like the **Asian Games**.
 
• **Online Money Gaming**: This involves staking money on an outcome. The bill subjects these services to high **taxation slabs** (e.g., 28 percent **GST** on the entry fee) and **Self-Regulatory Bodies (SRBs)** to ensure they do not facilitate **unorganized gambling**.
 
• **Nodal Ministry**: The **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)** is the designated authority responsible for drafting the rules and overseeing the compliance of **Intermediary Guidelines** for all online gaming platforms.

questions.question: 'Matki' is a popular folk dance performed in which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Matki** dance is a traditional folk dance primarily performed in the **Malwa region** of **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• This dance form is performed by women on various special occasions such as **weddings**, **festivals**, and to celebrate the **birth of a child**.
 
• The name of the dance is derived from the **matki** (earthen pot), which the dancers balance on their heads while performing intricate footwork and circular movements.
 
• It usually begins with a solo performance by a woman known as the **Jhela**, who is then joined by other dancers following her rhythm and lead.
 
• The performance is characterized by the use of the **Dhol**, a double-headed drum that provides the primary rhythmic beat for the dancers to maintain their balance and pace.
 
• The dancers wear traditional attire like the **lehenga** or **sari**, often embellished with ornaments that shimmer during the performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Andhra Pradesh**:

 
 
• Home to the classical dance **Kuchipudi** and folk forms such as **Lambadi**, **Dhimsa**, and **Veeranatyam**.
 
 
 
• **Lakshadweep**:
 
 
• Known for the **Lava dance**, a popular folk form performed by the people of **Minicoy Island**, and other dances like **Kolkali** and **Parichakali**.
 
 
 
• **West Bengal**:
 
 
• Famous for the **Chhau dance** (specifically the **Purulia** style), **Gambhira**, and the **Brita** dance, which is a traditional devotional form.

questions.question: In December 2024, which village was declared as India's first Border Solar Village?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Masali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Masali** village, situated in the **Jaisalmer district** of **Rajasthan**, achieved the historic milestone of being declared **India's first Border Solar Village** in **December 2024**.
 
• The village is located in close proximity to the **India-Pakistan international border**, making its transition to **renewable energy** a significant achievement for **national security** and **rural development**.
 
• This initiative involved the installation of comprehensive **Solar Photovoltaic (PV) systems**, including **solar rooftops** for every household and **solar-powered street lighting**, ensuring **24/7 electricity** supply in a historically power-deficit region.
 
• The project aims to reduce the carbon footprint of border settlements and align with the **Government of India's** vision of **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) by making remote areas energy independent.
 
• By providing reliable power, the government seeks to improve **telecommunication**, **education**, and **healthcare** services, thereby preventing migration from strategic **border areas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mana**:

 
 
• Located in the **Chamoli district** of **Uttarakhand**, it was formerly known as the last village of India but is now officially recognized as the **First Indian Village** at the **India-China border**.
 
 
 
• **Mawlynnong**:
 
 
• Situated in the **East Khasi Hills** of **Meghalaya**, this village is world-renowned for being **Asia's cleanest village** and is a model for **sustainable community tourism**.
 
 
 
• **Khonoma**:
 
 
• Located in **Nagaland**, it is distinguished as **India's first green village**, famous for its **Angami tribe's** efforts in **forest conservation** and the ban on hunting and logging since the late **1990s**.
 
 
 
• **Vibrant Villages Programme**:
 
 
• A centrally sponsored scheme launched to develop infrastructure and provide livelihood opportunities in villages along India's **Northern Border**, promoting **border security** through socio-economic development.

questions.question: In Tamil Nadu, the 'Pongal' festival is celebrated over how many days?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pongal** is a significant **harvest festival** celebrated by the Tamil community, primarily in the Indian state of **Tamil Nadu** and the Union Territory of **Puducherry**.
 
• The festival is observed to thank the **Sun God** (Surya) and nature for a bountiful harvest, marking the end of the winter solstice and the start of the sun's six-month-long journey northwards (**Uttarayanam**).
 
• It traditionally takes place over **four consecutive days** during the start of the Tamil month of **Thai**, which usually falls between **January 14 and January 17** every year.
 
• The four days of the festival are sequentially known as **Bhogi Pongal**, **Surya Pongal**, **Mattu Pongal**, and **Kaanum Pongal**, each involving distinct cultural and religious rituals.
 
• The term **Pongal** in Tamil translates to **boiling over** or spilling over, signifying the overflowing of **prosperity and abundance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The four-day celebration details:
 
 
• **Day 1: Bhogi Pongal** − People clean their homes and discard old belongings into a **bonfire**, symbolizing the removal of old habits and the embrace of new beginnings. It is dedicated to **Lord Indra**, the god of rain.
 
• **Day 2: Surya Pongal** − This is the main festival day where freshly harvested rice is boiled with **milk and jaggery** in a clay pot. When the mixture boils over, people shout **Pongalo Pongal**.
 
• **Day 3: Mattu Pongal** − Dedicated to **cattle**, especially bulls and cows that help farmers in the fields. Cattle are bathed, their horns are painted, and they are adorned with garlands. The traditional sport of **Jallikattu** often takes place on this day.
 
• **Day 4: Kaanum Pongal** − A day for **socializing and family reunions**. People visit relatives, parks, and beaches. The **Kaka Pidi Kanu Pidi** ritual is performed by women for the well-being of their brothers.

questions.question: The melting point of ice is ____ K.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**273.15**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **melting point** is the temperature at which a substance changes its state from **solid to liquid** at standard atmospheric pressure.
 
• On the **Celsius scale**, the melting point of pure ice is defined as **0°C** under a standard pressure of **1 atmosphere** (1 atm).
 
• The **Kelvin scale** is the **SI unit** of temperature, and the conversion between Celsius and Kelvin is given by the formula: **T(K) = t(°C) + 273.15**.
 
• By applying this relationship, the melting point of ice in Kelvin is calculated as **0 + 273.15 = 273.15 K**.
 
• Unlike the Celsius or Fahrenheit scales, the Kelvin scale is an **absolute scale** and does not use the degree symbol.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **373.15**:

 
 
• This value represents the **boiling point of water** on the Kelvin scale.
 
• It corresponds to **100°C** on the Celsius scale (100 + 273.15 = 373.15 K).
 
 
 
• **0**:
 
 
• On the Kelvin scale, **0 K** is known as **Absolute Zero**, the temperature at which all thermal motion of particles ceases.
 
• In Celsius, Absolute Zero is equivalent to **−273.15°C**.
 
 
 
• **100**:
 
 
• This is the numerical value for the **boiling point of water** in degrees **Celsius**.
 
• It marks the transition from the liquid phase to the gaseous phase at sea level.
 
 
 
• **Triple Point of Water**:
 
 
• Water can coexist in all three states (solid, liquid, and gas) at a specific temperature of **273.16 K** (0.01°C) and a partial vapor pressure of **611.657 Pascals**.

questions.question: When was the Pro Kabaddi League launched?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2014**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pro Kabaddi League (PKL)** was launched in **2014**, marking a significant milestone in the professionalization of the traditional Indian sport of Kabaddi.
 
• The league was established by **Mashal Sports**, a company co-founded by **Charu Sharma** and **Anand Mahindra**, and is currently managed by **Star India**.
 
• The first season commenced on **July 26, 2014**, featuring **eight teams** representing different Indian cities: Bengaluru, Delhi, Jaipur, Kolkata, Mumbai, Patna, Pune, and Vizag.
 
• The concept was influenced by the successful execution of the **Indian Premier League (IPL)** and the high viewership of Kabaddi during the **2006 Asian Games**.
 
• The league implemented a **caravan format**, which ensured that the matches were hosted in each of the home cities of the participating franchises.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inaugural Season Results**:

 
 
• The **Jaipur Pink Panthers**, owned by **Abhishek Bachchan**, became the **first-ever champions** of the league by defeating **U Mumba** in the final.
 
• The tournament gained massive popularity, becoming the **second most-watched** sports league in India after cricket.
 
 
 
• **Growth and Expansion**:
 
 
• While the league started with 8 teams, it expanded to **12 teams** in **2017** with the addition of franchises from Gujarat, Haryana, Tamil Nadu, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Key innovations introduced in the league include the **Do-or-Die Raid** (a mandatory point-scoring raid after two empty raids) and the **Super Tackle** (earning two points if three or fewer defenders tackle a raider).
 
• Prominent players such as **Pardeep Narwal**, known as the **Record Breaker**, and **Anup Kumar** became household names due to the league's success.

questions.question: Dhaka was the host of South Asian Federation Games in ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2010**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **11th edition** of the **South Asian Games**, which was historically known as the **South Asian Federation Games**, was hosted in **Dhaka**, **Bangladesh**, in **2010**.
 
• The multi-sport event took place from **January 29 to February 8, 2010**, marking the third time **Dhaka** served as the host city (previously in **1985** and **1993**).
 
• The official name of the competition was changed from the **South Asian Federation Games** to the **South Asian Games** in **2004**, though the older terminology is still frequently used in various contexts.
 
• A total of **eight nations** participated in the **2010 games**, including **Afghanistan**, **Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, **India**, **Maldives**, **Nepal**, **Pakistan**, and **Sri Lanka**.
 
• The **Bangabandhu National Stadium** in **Dhaka** was the primary venue for the opening and closing ceremonies, hosting thousands of athletes competing across **23 different sports**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Overview of the South Asian Games (SAG):**

 
 
• The games are a biennial multi-sport event held among the athletes from **South Asia**, governed by the **South Asian Olympic Council (SAOC)**.
 
• The **first edition** of the games was held in **Kathmandu**, **Nepal**, in **1984**.
 
• The objective of these games is to promote regional harmony and sporting excellence among the member nations of the **South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)** region.
 
 
 
• **Highlights of the 2010 Dhaka Games:**
 
 
• **India** maintained its dominance by topping the medal table with **90 gold**, **55 silver**, and **30 bronze** medals.
 
• The host nation, **Bangladesh**, achieved its most successful performance in the history of the games at that time, securing the **third position** with **18 gold medals**.
 
• The official mascot of the **2010 South Asian Games** was **Kutumb**, a representation of the **Magpie Robin** (Doyel), which is the national bird of **Bangladesh**.

questions.question: The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction agreement is an international treaty under the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**UNCLOS**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ)** agreement, commonly referred to as the **High Seas Treaty**, is an international legally binding instrument established under the framework of the **United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS)**.
 
• Its primary objective is the **conservation** and **sustainable use** of marine biological diversity in areas that lie beyond the **Exclusive Economic Zones (EEZ)** and continental shelves of coastal states, which encompass approximately **64 percent** of the ocean surface.
 
• The treaty was officially adopted on **June 19, 2023**, after nearly **20 years** of discussions and negotiations to address legal gaps in **global ocean governance**.
 
• It operates on four key pillars: the **sharing of benefits** from **Marine Genetic Resources (MGRs)**; the use of **Area-Based Management Tools (ABMTs)**, including **Marine Protected Areas (MPAs)**; the conduct of **Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs)** for deep-sea activities; and **Capacity Building and the Transfer of Marine Technology (CBTMT)** to assist developing nations.
 
• The **BBNJ** is considered the **third implementing agreement** under **UNCLOS**, following the **1994 Part XI Agreement** and the **1995 Fish Stocks Agreement**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNCLOS (United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea)**:

 
 
• Adopted in **1982** and effective from **1994**, it is often called the **Constitution of the Oceans**.
 
• It defines the **legal status** of various maritime zones, including **Territorial Seas** (up to **12 nautical miles**) and **EEZs** (up to **200 nautical miles**).
 
 
 
• **UNESCO (United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization)**:
 
 
• While it hosts the **Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission (IOC)**, which provides scientific data for the **BBNJ**, it is not the governing body for this specific treaty.
 
 
 
• **WTO (World Trade Organization)**:
 
 
• An organization focused on **global trade rules** and dispute resolution; it does not possess jurisdiction over **maritime biological conservation**.

questions.question: The International IP Index 2025 is which edition of the index?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International IP Index 2025** represents the **13th edition** of the annual report produced by the **U.S. Chamber of Commerce Global Innovation Policy Center (GIPC)**.
 
• The index serves as a comprehensive roadmap for nations seeking to improve their **intellectual property (IP)** frameworks to drive **economic growth**, **innovation**, and **technological advancement**.
 
• It evaluates the IP climate of the world leading economies using a set of **50 unique indicators** that span across several critical categories of protection.
 
• Since its inception in **2012**, the index has become a primary benchmark for investors and policymakers to assess the **legal certainty** and **market environment** for creative and innovative industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evaluation Framework:**

 
 
• The index benchmarks economies across nine distinct categories, including **Patents**, **Copyrights**, **Trademarks**, **Design Rights**, and **Trade Secrets**.
 
• It also scrutinizes the **Commercialization of IP Assets**, **Enforcement mechanisms**, **Systemic Efficiency**, and the ratification of **International Treaties**.
 
 
 
• **Global Coverage:**
 
 
• The previous **12th edition** (released in 2024) analyzed **55 global economies**, which collectively account for over **90%** of the world **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**.
 
• The report highlights how robust **IP standards** correlate with higher levels of **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** and increased **Research and Development (R&D)** activities.
 
• In the Indian context, the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)** under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry** monitors such indices to align domestic policies with global best practices.

questions.question: As per the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index 2023, India moved up to ____ rank in the Global Ranking in International Shipments category.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**22nd**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **World Bank Logistics Performance Index (LPI) 2023**, India achieved a significant milestone by jumping to the **22nd** rank in the **International Shipments** category.
 
• This specific rank marks a massive improvement of 22 spots compared to the **2018 LPI report**, where India was positioned at **44th** in the same category.
 
• The **International Shipments** indicator measures the ease of arranging competitively priced shipments, a factor crucial for **export-led growth** and global trade integration.
 
• This progress is largely attributed to the government's focus on **logistics efficiency** through the **PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan** and the **National Logistics Policy (2022)**.
 
• India's rank in **Logistics Competence and Quality** also saw an upward trajectory, reaching the **38th** position in 2023 compared to 42nd in 2018.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Logistics Performance Index (LPI) 2023**:

 
 
• The 2023 report, titled **Connecting to Compete**, is the **7th edition** and assesses **139 countries**.
 
• India's **overall rank** in the LPI 2023 is **38th**, an improvement from 44th in 2018 and 54th in 2014.
 
• The LPI is based on six core components: **Customs**, **Infrastructure**, **International Shipments**, **Logistics Competence**, **Tracking and Tracing**, and **Timeliness**.
 
• In **Infrastructure**, India climbed from 52nd in 2018 to **47th** in 2023 due to investments in **port modernization** and **dedicated freight corridors**.
 
• India ranked **35th** for **Timeliness** and **38th** for **Tracking and Tracing**, reflecting advancements in **digitalization** and **supply chain visibility**.
 
• The report noted that **technology-driven initiatives** like the **Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP)** have been instrumental in reducing delays.
